sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Erev Shabbat Kodesh Parshat Chayei Sarah,
26 Marcheshvan 5716*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse "Ashrei tevchar v'tekarev" is recited before circumcision, corresponding to four levels, and that circumcision draws down from above the chain of descent.

translations.translation: "Ashrei tevchar v'tekarev yishkon chatsereicha, nisbe'ah b'tuv beitecha, kedosh heichalecha"1,
Now, this verse is recited before the covenant of circumcision,
as it is brought in the Siddur, the order of circumcision.
And the source for this is what is stated in the Zohar2:
"The early pious ones... when they would bring their sons for this sacrifice, they would open and say, 'Ashrei tevchar v'tekarev yishkon chatsereicha...'"
[And although in the Zohar there it says "the early pious ones," etc.,
the Alter Rebbe wrote in his Siddur3
that this is a matter equal for every soul.]
And the explanation of the connection of this verse to the covenant of circumcision is,
that in this verse four matters are enumerated:
"Chatzereicha" (your courtyards) in the plural, two aspects of courtyard4,
"Beitecha" (your house), and "Heichalecha" (your palace).
And the order of the matters in the verse is from below upward.
As it is brought in the Zohar there,
"First 'chatzereicha,' then 'beitecha,' and then 'heichalecha,'
this one is more internal than that one, and this one is higher than that one."
And it can be said,
that these four matters correspond to the four worlds of Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah (ABiYA)
(as will be explained below, section 6).
Therefore, this verse is recited before the circumcision,
for through circumcision there is a drawing down from above the chain of descent,
and in order for this drawing down to be, there must first be the completeness of the chain of descent
(the four worlds)
as will be explained below
(section 7).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the difference between a courtyard and a house, and between a covered and uncovered courtyard, in simple terms and in halachah.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
that the difference between a courtyard and a house
(in their simple sense)
is,
that a house is a person's dwelling, and in the courtyard are found the animals and birds,
as it is brought in the Mishnah5:
"If one would place an animal in the courtyard... and raise chickens"6.
And within the courtyard itself there are two types:
a covered courtyard and an uncovered courtyard.
For the difference between a covered courtyard and an uncovered courtyard is also in halachah:
An uncovered courtyard
(when it is more than two se'ah, by Torah law it is a private domain, but by rabbinic law it is a karmelit, because it resembles a public domain7),
and a covered courtyard is a private domain even by rabbinic law8.
And the difference between them simply,
is that the guarding of animals is also in an uncovered courtyard
[and it only requires that the courtyard be surrounded by partitions],
and the guarding of birds
(which can fly over the partitions)
is specifically in a covered courtyard.
